params.linkText: Why is DOW stock trading lower?

children: UBS Target Cut and Market Context
The selling pressure follows an update early Friday from
analyst Joshua Spector, who maintained a Neutral rating on the materials science company while lowering his 12-month price target from $32 to $30.

The target reduction aligns closely with widely reported macroeconomic headwinds currently facing Dow and its peers. The chemicals sector is navigating a slower-than-anticipated recovery in global industrial demand, which continues to constrain pricing power across core segments.

Prolonged industrial weakness in Europe and a lack of robust economic stimulus from China are weighing heavily on global polyethylene margins. The revised $30 target likely reflects trimmed near-term EBITDA estimates tied to customer destocking and elevated raw material costs, which are widely expected to keep the company’s operating leverage constrained through the end of the year.

With crude oil and naphtha feedstock prices remaining volatile amid Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions, commodity chemical producers like Dow are finding it increasingly difficult to pass elevated input costs down to end-market consumers.
Dow shares were down 2.66% at $27.80 at the time of publication on Friday,
